method.summary: Reconcile the public Woodhouse project records to a dated operator-reviewed snapshot, then independently request every live entry point, read only build identities the apps publish themselves, and check public repository heads. Private repository contents, HEADs and commit history are not published.

snapshot.repositoryPolicy: Private repository contents are not published or connected to this endpoint. A project whose repository is public is summarised from that repository and its published site.

method.liveRequests: Each entry point was requested with GET, redirects followed, User-Agent AppComposer-Inventory/1.0 (+https://composer.loftwah.com), timeout 25s. Status, final URL and document title were recorded. A non-2xx response is not counted as a live entry point.
method.repositoryChecks: Public repository heads were read with `git ls-remote https://github.com/loftwah/<repo>.git HEAD`; private repositories are marked private and no head is recorded.
method.identityChecks: Deployed source identity is recorded only where the running app publishes it (`/build.json`, `/healthz` or a build meta tag). No deployment was inferred from a repository head.
boundaries: No credential, token, cookie, private issue/PR body, private repository name or private commit history is recorded.
A blueprint pin is a declared brief revision, not a claim about what production currently runs.
Unknown values stay unknown with the observation that made them unknown; no old value is copied forward.

projects.name: Bubbles
projects.summary: Bubbles is an arcade bubble shooter you play in the browser or on your phone: line up a shot, match three or more and clear the board. It’s for anyone who wants a quick round that feels good on a small screen.
projects.current: Fewest Shots is live as a second competitive mode: one board, no shot limit, cleared in as few shots as possible. Submitted runs are replayed on the server to derive the result, so a record cannot come from a browser's unverified claim, and a genuine long clear stays eligible. The same work corrected an advertised 30-shot objective that did not match the real scoring. The live build also carries the promoted Bubblecap mascot and reworked presentation from the same window.
projects.nextProof: Watch whether the new mode produces repeat attempts and honest records from players beyond factory testing, and finish the held product work. Physical-phone and final visual acceptance remain separate observations.
projects.proofBoundary: The deployed game build contains Fewest Shots and the replay verifier is reviewed source; this record did not complete a fresh human playthrough. A working competition mode is not a player community, an audience or evidence of demand, and record persistence depends on the game's own service.

projects.name: Protocol 11

projects.summary: Protocol 11 is a card game for two to four players around one table, played solo or with friends. Twelve stages and a cast of characters make a house you play through, and every round brings a new Protocol.
projects.current: An illegal desktop drop now refuses visibly instead of silently doing nothing: the destination answers with a marked refusal, ownership and the turn stay unchanged, and a legal drop still works. The same delivery reworked Wild placement and hand sorting, gave Journey stages distinct configurations, and corrected the production mix on three campaign films. The climax, decision short and rival-threat short are public with a press page and source records, and Woodhouse keeps an account-free download of the pack.
